doc.name: Quicktron C56 with suction cup (DFW6 relay storage VTM)

$comment: The VTM that works DFW6's relay storage aisles, 40 in the map as 'VTM (vacuum)'. Figures are the bot specifications Vinay directed on 2026-09-21, from GreyOrange's hardware team (docs/walmart-facts.md section 6b): provisional, 'to be used for this week' while HAI vetting is in progress. The model is disputed: MOM Day 1 says a suction-cup C56, and Vinay asks 'A42T vacuum vtm?'. Height bears on it: DFW6's top storage level sits near 9.4 m (23 levels from 800 mm, 390.9 mm apart; facts file section 2); the matrix's plain C56 builds are customisable from 2 m to 7 m, its tallest C56 (the Boots C56-ST) stands 9.137 m, and HAI's A42T reaches 12 m. The matrix's C56-S-2D column differs from the directive: 600 mm/s² acceleration, a 1.8 m/s laden speed, and turns of 3.2 s and 6.4 s.

body.$comment: The C56-S-2D column of the Ranger Relay Profile Matrix as transcribed on equipment/world-protocol-0.8, its lengths read as tenths of a millimetre. Its height is customisable from 2 m to 7 m, and DFW6's build is not stated.

floor_drive.$comment: The directive states no turn times, and the simulator needs none: it keeps DFW6's VTMs in their aisles.

lift.$comment: The directive gives one VTM speed and acceleration; the simulator applies them to the lift as well, which is still to be confirmed.
